newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour sees possible delay on EU currency.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour sees possible delay on EU currency.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party cast doubt on Sunday on the prospect of Britain joining a single European currency during the next parliament.

The party, which is widely tipped to win power in a May 1 election, has said there are "formidable obstacles" to Britain being in the first wave of membership if it goes ahead as planned in January 1999.
But Labour foreign affairs spokesman Robin Cook appeared to go further on Sunday, saying: "If you didn't join in 1999, it is unlikely you would be joining in the course of the next parliament."

"In the event that Britain doesn't join in the first wave, while we will continue to review this and look carefully at the figures, I would have thought the probability is that one is looking towards the subsequent parliament," he said in an interview on London Weekend Television.
